doc.title: Phoebe Jacobs and Jackie Harris interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 21, 2006

title: The Society of Singers
summary: Jacobs explains how Ella and Sinatra's idea became the Society of Singers and its 'Ella' award gala.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Gee. I was interested to see you also have some involvement with the Society of Singers where our good friend Joe Williams received a —

Yes he did, an honor one year. Well the Society of Singers started because Ella Fitzgerald and Frank Sinatra used to be approached by singers in need. Like Louis Armstrong and Duke and many of them were approached by musicians in need. And they decided it would be a wonderful thing if they could get something going where a singer could, with some dignity, could approach an organization and get some help. So a man by the name of Bud Granoff, who used to work for Frank Sinatra, was a very successful publisher married to a lady by the name of Kitty Kallen. And they got together with Ella and Frank to form the Society of Singers in Hollywood. Of course after a couple of months and some internal problems they retired from it but not until Buddy Granoff got all the singers that were interested, like Bing Crosby, Helen O’Connell, Tony Bennett, Peggy Lee, all to give a duty — no wait a minute, that’s not the word I want — doing royalty- free permission to release their hit record and he put it on one LP and all the proceeds was going to the Society of Singers. And then they decided on the gala, of course they got Merv Griffin, you know Merv Griffin used to be a band singer. So they got Merv Griffin to give them the ballroom of the Beverly Hilton Hotel in Los Angeles where they did a fundraiser and instead of giving out a Tony or an Oscar they gave out an Ella. And I, having worked for Ella and Peggy and all these people, I volunteered to be part of that. So I still — I’m not as active as I was but I still proceed to do whatever I can.
Yeah. Well it sounds like your calendar is always full to me. When I look at the things that both of you are doing. © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-
